keywords_required:
Secondary industries are manufacturing industries [1] that change raw materials into
finished or semi-finished products [1].
[Max 1 mark]

Tertiary industries are those that provide services to people and businesses [1], such
as retailing/education/healthcare/banking [1].
[Max 1 mark]

Primary industries declined by almost 90 per cent, from over 50 per cent to just over 5 per
cent [1]. Secondary industries increased by over a half, from about 14 per cent to about
24 per cent [1]. Tertiary employment doubled, from about 35 per cent to about 70 per
cent [1].
[Max 3 marks]

Changes in employment structure may have occurred due to: greater access to
technology allowing the country to move away from primary industries [1]; a more skilled
workforce [1]; government incentives to develop manufacturing and services [1];
development of export-oriented industries, e.g. vehicle manufacturing [1] rather than
industries for the domestic market, e.g. food and drink industries [1].
[Max 3 marks]

The increasing interconnectedness of the world through economic, cultural and political
links.
[1 mark]

TNCs have operations in many countries [1]. Often, their research and development is
located in HICs, but their assembly plants are located in LICs/MICs [1]. They may use LICs
for sources of cheap labour and raw materials [1], but many of the products are sold in
HICs as these countries have more profitable markets than in LICs [1].         [Max 3 marks]

The impact of globalisation at a local scale may include: small businesses may find it
hard to compete with major global companies [1]; closure of a TNC branch plant can cause
local unemployment [1]; the population of local communities may become multicultural [1];
consumers may have a greater choice of goods, e.g. food [1]; families are more likely to
spread to other countries due to migration [1]; the cost of overseas travel may be
reduced [1].
[Max 5 marks]

Positive aspects of TNCs on host countries may include the creation of jobs/provision
of more wages in a community; an inflow of capital to promote economic growth; the
transfer of technological skills; more revenue for the government from taxes and royalties.
Negative impacts of TNCs may include economic dependence on the TNC; flows of
government funding away from other sectors in order to provide incentives for TNCs;
